basis: Congenital inward turning of the eyelid; an ocular structural disorder.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising primarily in skin; lymphoma warrants both haematologic and infectious_immune axes.
Multiple meningeal tumors at the skull base; location alone does not establish bone or cranial sensory-organ damage.
Hereditary autonomic paraganglial neuroendocrine tumor syndrome, chiefly head and neck; ear, airway and renal damage are not established as common.
Sensory-autonomic neuropathy with defining hypohidrosis; corneal scarring affects 15/20 (75%). Recurrent skin infections do not establish primary immunodeficiency.
Integumentary malignancy supports the skin axis; breast and Bartholin gland subtypes do not supply additional axes.
Ependymal tumor arising in the central nervous system, commonly the spinal cord.
Inherited autoinflammatory syndrome umbrella; persistent damage to another organ is not established across most subtypes.
Chronic immune-mediated transmural intestinal inflammation; individual extraintestinal organ complications do not consistently meet the 30% threshold.
Defined by brain abnormalities, severe developmental delay and intellectual disability; facial dysmorphism alone does not establish another damaged organ.
Secundum atrial septal defect defines cardiac involvement; unspecified noncardiac defects do not justify additional axes.
Plasmalogen synthesis defect with severe neurologic disease (3/3) and cataracts (2/3); skeletal dysplasia ancestry lacks supporting skeletal phenotypes.
Benign tumor of chest-wall supporting tissues; thoracic location does not establish lung involvement.
ACTA1 skeletal myopathy; respiratory and bulbar weakness arise from muscle disease. Cardiomyopathy is occasional (5-29%).
Developmental brain disorder and primary hypogonadism define the syndrome; clubfeet and skeletal maturation defects occur in 80-99%. Infections alone do not prove immunodeficiency.
Latent mycobacterial infection without active organ disease; future tuberculosis reactivation is a risk, not current pulmonary damage.
Generalized joint laxity with recurrent or congenital dislocations; no common extra-articular organ damage is established.
Organic acidemia; developmental disability and thrombocytopenia each occur in 30-79%. Renal dysfunction is listed at 5-29%; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Pathologic TDP-43 inclusions damage brain and spinal neurons and glia; proteostasis ancestry alone does not establish a clinical metabolic disorder.
Autoimmune exocrine-disease umbrella; salivary, lacrimal and hepatic targets vary by subtype, with no single anatomical axis established across most patients.
Heart failure due to immune-mediated rheumatic cardiac damage; congestion alone does not establish intrinsic pulmonary or hepatic injury.
Childhood lymphoid-cell malignancy; lymphoma warrants haematologic and infectious_immune axes. No extranodal organ is consistently affected across the umbrella.
Odontogenic cyst attached to an unerupted or partially erupted tooth; teeth and associated oral tissues fall within gastrointestinal.
Localized hamartomatous malformation of eccrine sweat glands, which are skin appendages.
Adrenal aldosterone excess defines endocrine disease; directly mediated hypertension is common (>30%). Secondary forms make its frequency variable.
